No Possible Move 4 Player Actions 5 Placement Rules (Summary) 6 Game End 7 Scoring Summary 8 Turn Summary VIZIA Objective Score the most points by forming hexagons of 6 tiles and claiming them with your markers. Scoring: 6 different colors = 3 points 2 alternating colors = 2 points any other hexagon = 1 point Game end: a player places all markers OR all tiles have been played Game Overview Play proceeds clockwise. A turn consists of: Play tiles (at least 1) optionally play additional tiles optionally refill hand refill shared display A player may end their turn at any time after playing at least one tile. Turn Structure 1. Play Tiles The active player must play at least 1 tile. Tiles may be played from: personal hand shared display any combination Additional tiles may optionally be played. Placement rules: first tile: placed freely all further tiles: must be adjacent colors must be neighbors on the color wheel Color Adjacency Green ↔ Yellow / Blue Blue ↔ Green / Purple Purple ↔ Blue / Red Red ↔ Purple / Orange Orange ↔ Red / Yellow Yellow ↔ Orange / Green 2. Complete a Hexagon When a hexagon of 6 tiles is completed: active player places their marker inside marker remains until game end multiple hexagons may be completed in one turn 3. Continue Playing Tiles (Optional) The player may: play additional tiles complete multiple hexagons voluntarily end the turn The turn ends when: player stops OR no legal placements remain 4. Refill Hand (Optional) After placing tiles, the player may: take tiles from the display refill up to hand limit or skip Then: refill shared display 5. No Possible Move If a player cannot place a tile: reveal hand turn is skipped replace the entire display Player Actions During your turn: Required: play at least 1 tile Optional: play additional tiles use tiles from display complete multiple hexagons refill hand end turn early If blocked: pass (after showing hand) Placement Rules (Summary) tiles must be adjacent colors must be neighbors any number of tiles per turn hexagon = exactly 6 tiles completing player claims hexagon Game End The game ends immediately when: a player places all markers OR no tiles remain Then: count points highest score wins tie: most hexagons wins Scoring Summary 6 colors = 3 points 2 alternating colors = 2 points otherwise = 1 point Turn Summary play 1+ tiles claim completed hexagon(s) optionally play more optionally refill hand refill display next player Board Game Arena would like to thank MJ Games for making it possible to have this game here. 2332 vizia العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti keel فارسی Suomi Français Galego עברית Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Bahasa Indonesia 日本語 한국어 Lietuvių Latviešu Bahasa Malaysia Nederlands Norsk Polski Português Română Русский язык Slovenčina Slovenščina Српски Svenska ไทย Türkçe Українська мова Tiếng Việt 中文 (漢) 中文 (汉) Application loading... ... {DISPLAY_IN_OTHER_LANG} {LANG_REDIRECT_CODE} boardgamearena.com Top Help What is Board Game Arena? [Rating: 4/10] Not a fan of this abstract game. Highly AP prone that just made the game move too slowly. There is also some luck of the draw that probably could be worked around with more experience, but there will still always be some luck. Also, the components are awful!

[Rating: 5/10] It's pretty and I want to like it more because my wife bought it for me as an impluse purchase, but it's just an OK abstract. I don't think the decisions are super compelling, but at least the game is short and the rules are simple enough to be able to reach both gamers and non-gamers alike.

[Rating: 7/10] Very cool abstract placement game with a multitude of scoring. The randomness of the draw is not too big a factor and the fact that it plays up to 4 is a big plus. It's a great idea that would be better in a nicer edition.  Update - The quality of the pocket version is just abysmal.  Don't get tricked into buying it; the full version is worth whatever price is asked.

[Rating: 7/10] £3 FLGS buy!  Great little abstract, with good basic rules and advanced options as well.  Tiny box, and suspect quality of components, but for the money can't complain...

[Rating: 7/10] Random and lightweight tile-laying game. With lots of optional rules that don't change the game much.  What's good about it? It's easy to learn, it's beautiful and the rule almost feels so natural. I think these are signs of a good game of this category.

[Rating: 8/10] Neat abstract game.  has some interesting variants too. components could have been better but it was cheap.  would buy again if it was made with plastic bits.
